clinician.trajectory_summary: The 30-year-old male initially presented with hemoptysis (50-100 ml of bloody sputum), paroxysmal chest distress, shortness of breath, and palpitations. Initial pulmonary CT showed mild infection, later normalized. Abdominal ultrasound and echocardiography were normal at first presentation. The clinical course improved after antibiotic and hemostatic therapy. No documented episodes of hypertension, headaches, or sweating were reported to support catecholamine excess. No biochemical testing or adrenal imaging results confirming pheochromocytoma nor pathology confirming alveolar hemorrhage were disclosed in the reviewed reports or source documents.
